title: Delimiter smoothing and atomic function-call window for SSE streams
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Context: We continue to see production incidents where high-frequency small SSE fragments lead to duplicate delimiters or mid-JSON emission that downstream OpenAI-compat clients reassemble incorrectly. This PR implements a two-part mitigation: (1) a delimiter smoother (a tiny, adaptive jitter buffer) that coalesces micro-fragments and reduces delimiter churn while preserving end-to-end latency SLOs, and (2) an atomic function-call window that defers final delimiter emission for a short, bounded period while fncall payloads are completed, ensuring structured function call frames are emitted as contiguous, reassemblable spans.

Motivation: avoid partial JSON reconstruction failures and duplicated trailing delimiters in low-latency workloads (chat streaming, tool-calling) without regressing throughput.

Implementation summary:
- Introduced sse/stream/delim_smoother.go (runtime component) that maintains a per-connection micro-buffer with adaptive delay based on recent fragment inter-arrival statistics and sequence entropy heuristics. Delay bounds are conservative: default max 12ms, min 0ms; the smoother is bypassed for long frames to avoid unnecessary buffering.
- Added sse/stream/fncall_window.go which tags fncall sentinel starts and holds terminal delimiter emission until either a local completion event arrives or the fncall window timeout elapses (configurable, default 40ms). This guarantees atomic emission of structured fncall outputs and reduces the need for downstream heuristics.
- OpenAI compatibility layer: updated openai_compat/sse_decoder.go to understand the fncall atomic markers and to treat them as a single assembly unit when reconstructing JSON objects for older clients.
- Tests: added unit tests for fragment coalescing, fncall-window edge cases, and integration tests simulating bursty micro-fragments and delayed fncall payloads.
- Metrics and observability: added metrics sse.delim_smoother.delay_ms{p50,p95}, sse.fncall.window_hold_count, and an opt-in trace span to the console for troubleshooting.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4521)
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Benchmarked end-to-end latency (p95 increased by <2ms in worst-case synthetic workloads, CPU overhead <1% at 1k rps)
- [x] Docs updated (streaming stability notes)
- [x] Feature flagged and configurable via runtime flags and per-tenant policy

Notes on behavior/compatibility:
- Default configuration is conservative; smoothing is opt-in per-tenant for Dedicated/Private initially to gather telemetry.
- The fncall atomic window is enabled by default in hosted to protect common tool-calling flows; it has a runtime toggle for immediate rollback.
- This change does not alter wire protocol or API surface; clients that already handle partial JSON are unaffected.

- Noah: found a race in the fncall window when a fncall completion and connection close race; author fixed by making the window logic idempotent and added test coverage.

Configurable and feature-flagged; no API changes."
